dossier.public_summary: The 13-day dip has a very strong secondary eclipse (~35% as deep as the primary) and out-of-transit swings about half the dip depth, plus wildly varying depths between sectors. The star also shows large astrometric excess and RV amplitude. Together this is best explained as an eclipsing binary on the target, not a 1.8-Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: A second dip well above brightening (snr >5) at phase 0.7091 is about 1/3.6 of the planetoid dip depth. A planet would not show a ~116 ppm secondary near secondary_over_bump 1.485; this depth and SNR match an eclipsing binary where primary and secondary are both stellar.

Large out-of-transit modulation at this period (~half the dip depth) indicates ellipsoidal/beaming or spot modulation from a close binary, not a quiet planet host, consistent with phase-curve as binary sign.

Depth changes both between and within the same pipeline (TESS-SPOC p_constant 5.48e-05, SPOC 2-min p_constant 0.004). A true planet depth should be steady; sector-dependent change favours a blended/eclipsing binary where aperture contamination changes.
